'''Martin Schütz''' (14 November 1963 – 25 February 2018) was a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[Theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]] and [[Quantum chemistry|quantum chemist]].<ref name=MSlautHumUni>{{cite web |title=Martin Schütz|url= https://www.chemie.hu-berlin.de/de/forschung/theoretische-chemie/ag_schuetz |publisher=Mathematisch-Naturwissenschaftliche Fakultät, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin |accessdate=22 May 2021}}</ref><ref name=MSlautR>{{cite web |url= https://lcams2019.wixsite.com/home/martin-schuetz-1 |publisher=University of Regensburg, Bavaria |title=Martin Schütz 14.11.1963 – 25.02.2018 |work=Local correlation approaches for molecules and solids |accessdate=22 May 2021}}</ref><ref name= MSlautKreisTheoChem>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Martin Schütz |work=Curriculum Vitae |url=http://www-schuetz.chemie.uni-regensburg.de/index.php?id=108 |publisher=Universität Regensburg (Arbeitskreis Theoretische Chemie) |accessdate=22 May 2021}}</ref>

== Life ==
Martin Schütz was born at [[Burgdorf, Switzerland|Burgdorf]] ([[Canton of Bern|BE]]) in [[Swiss Plateau|Middle Switzerland]], the son of Jakob and Sylvia Schütz.<ref name=MSlautHumUni/>

His first year of university level education was spent studying [[Electrical Engineering]] at [[Zürich]]'s [[ETH Zurich|ETH (Technology Institute)]] during 1983/84. He then switched to the [[University of Bern]] where he studied [[Physical Chemistry]] between 1984 and 1989, receiving his first degree on 25 May 1989 in exchange for a dissertation entitled "Laser spectroscopy and Monte Carlo simulations of molecular solvent clusters".<ref name=MSlautR/>   He stayed on at [[University of Bern|Bern]] undertaking research for his doctorate which he received on 13 May 1993. This time his work was concerned with investigating "vibronic effects in hydrate clusters":  the resulting dissertation was entitled "Structures and Vibrations of Hydrate clusters with aromatic Chromophores". Schütz's work was supervised by Prof. Samuel Leutwyler, both in respect of the dissertation with which he completed his first degree course and for his doctorate.<ref name=MSlautR/>   There was still much about his doctoral work that remained experimental, and his next research priority involved a focus on the underlying theory.<ref name=MSlautHumUni/>

Schütz now returned to the [[ETH Zurich|Technology Institute]] at [[Zürich]] where he spent the year 1993/94 in a supportive role at the Interdisciplinary Project Centre for Super Computers.<ref name=MSbijETH>{{cite journal |author1=Wim Klopper|author2=Martin Schütz|author3=Hans P. Lüthi |title=An ''ab initio'' derived torsional potential energy surface for (H2O)3. II. Benchmark studies and interaction energies |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |year=1995 |volume=103 |issue=3 |pages=1085–1098 |doi=10.1063/1.470701 |bibcode=1995JChPh.103.1085K |url=https://doi.org/10.1063/1.470701 |accessdate=22 May 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref>   In 1994 he accepted an opportunity to move to [[Sweden]] where he joined the group working with [[:de:Björn O. Roos|Björn Roos]] at [[Lund University]], just outside [[Malmö]] in the extreme south of the country. He remained at Lund with a post-doctoral fellowship for three years, working on the development of integral-direct correlation methodologies.<ref name=AppsinChemlautMSuRL>{{cite book |title=Applications in Chemistry .... An Integral Direct, Distributed-Data, Parallel MP2 Algorithm |author1=Martin Schütz  |author2=Roland Lindh  |pages=127–132 |url=https://www.pdc.kth.se/polopoly_fs/1.764055.1600689184!/PDC_Progress_Report_1994-1996.pdf |work=Progress Report 1994 – 1996  |isbn=91-7170-695-X |date=November 1996 |publisher=PDC Parallelldatorcentrum, Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm |accessdate=22 May 2021}}</ref><ref name=LokKorr>{{cite web |work=Lokale Korrelations-methoden |title=Von kanonischen zu lokalen Orbitalen |pages=328–329 |author=Martin Schütz |date=March 2003 |url=https://www.gdch.de/fileadmin/downloads/Publikationen/Nachrichten_aus_der_Chemie/PDFs/Trendberichte_2003/korrel.pdf |publisher=Gesellschaft Deutscher Chemiker e.V.(Theoretische Chemie magazine), Frankfurt am Main |accessdate=22 May 2021}}</ref>   In 1996 Schütz and his fellow researcher Roland Lindh received the SUP’Prize at the SUP'EUR 96 "computing in science" event at [[Kraków]] in recognition of the work.<ref name=PreislautPDC>{{cite web |title=Sup'Prize to PDC users  |work=PDC Newsletter  |date=September 1996  |pages=1, 3–5  |url= https://www.kth.se/polopoly_fs/1.744616.1600689163!/Newsletter1996-1.pdf  |issn=1401-9671  |publisher=PDC, KTH, Stockholm  |accessdate=22 May 2021}}</ref>   He moved closer to home in 1997 when he joined the group working with [[:de:Hans-Joachim Werner (Chemiker) |Hans-Joachim Werner]] at [[University of Stuttgart|Stuttgart]].<ref name=UmAnaEneGralautMSuHJW>{{cite journal |title=Analytical energy gradients for local second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory using density fitting approximations |url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.1760747 |date=April 2004 |author1=Martin Schütz |author2=Hans-Joachim Werner  |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |volume=121 |issue=2 |pages=737–750 |doi=10.1063/1.1760747 |pmid=15260600 |bibcode=2004JChPh.121..737S |accessdate=22 May 2021|url-access=subscription }}</ref>   It was at [[University of Stuttgart|Stuttgart]] that on 15 February 2001 Schütz received his [[Habilitation |habilitation (higher post-graduate degree)]] for work on "Electron Correlation in Large Molecular Systems: From Integral-Direct to Linear Scaling Local Correlation Methods", following which he accepted a lectureship at the university.<ref name= MSlautKreisTheoChem/>

In 2004 Schütz was appointed to a full professorship in [[Theoretical Chemistry]] at the [[University of Regensburg]].<ref name=MSlautR/>   He moved on again in 2016, accepting the professorship in [[Theoretical Chemistry]] at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]] which became vacant through the retirement of [[Joachim Sauer |Professor Emeritus Joachim Sauer]].<ref name=MSlautHumUni/>

Martin Schütz was only 54 when he died from illness, surrounded by his family, on 25 February 2018.<ref name=MSlautHumUni/>

== Works ==
The principal focus of Schütz's research was on "ab initio calculations" of the electronic structures of extended molecules (local correlation methods),<ref name=LokKorr/> [[Excited state|excited electronic states]], and [[Intermolecular force|intermolecular forces]].<ref name=UmForschungMS>{{cite web |title=Forschung |date=11 February 2020 |url= https://www.chemie.hu-berlin.de/de/forschung/theoretische-chemie/ag_usvyat/forschung |work=Ressources ... Martin Schütz |publisher= Mathematisch-Naturwissenschaftliche Fakultät (Naturwissenschaftliche Fakultät Institut .... Theoretiesche Chemie), Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin |accessdate=23 May 2021}}</ref>   During his time at [[University of Stuttgart |Stuttgart]] he successfully developed correlation methods scaled in a linear sequence according to molecule size, building on work undertaken by [[Peter Pulay]] during the 1980s. The work that Schütz undertook during the first couple of years of the third millennium invokes [[Post–Hartree–Fock|Post–Hartree–Fock methodologies]], applying [[coupled cluster]] techniques, and extending to molecules with triple substitutions. Previously they had been limited to small molecules because of the absence of scalability of the methods conditioned by cononinical (and therefore not localised) orthogonal molecular orbital bases.<ref name="Zaleśny p. ">{{cite book | last=Zaleśny | first=Robert | title=Linear-scaling techniques in computational chemistry and physics : methods and applications | publisher=Springer | publication-place=Dordrecht | date=2011 | isbn=978-90-481-2852-5 | oclc=719363166 | pages=345–407}}</ref>
